description:
Stafford Gray is seeking experienced Power Pages and Dynamics 365 developers to help build a modernized claims processing system for a Florida state agency. The project replaces a legacy system with Microsoft Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Dataverse, and Azure Government, including a secure portal for external claimants and internal staff. We are hiring for two positions.
 This is a fully remote contract role with an expected implementation of about two years.
 Responsibilities:
 Design, build, and maintain Power Pages portals for anonymous and authenticated external users and internal staff
 Customize Dynamics 365 tables, forms, views, business rules, and workflows that support claims processing
 Build pages, forms, and lists using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Liquid templates
 Configure portal authentication, table permissions, and role-based access
 Implement document upload and handling within the portal
 Integrate portal and CRM functionality with Dataverse, Azure services, and APIs
 Build accessible portals that meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards
 Support data migration, testing, UAT, deployment, and documentation
 
 Requirements 
 Required:
 4+ years of hands-on Power Pages or Power Apps Portals development
 Experience customizing Dynamics 365 CE or model-driven Power Apps on Dataverse
 Strong HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Liquid templating skills
 Experience configuring portal authentication with Azure AD B2C or Microsoft Entra External ID
 Experience with Power Automate and integrating with backend systems and APIs
 Must be based in the U.S.
 Available for contract work; we work directly with candidates, not through third-party vendors
 
 Preferred:
 PL-400 or PL-200 certification
 Experience with WCAG 2.1 AA accessible portal design
 Experience with claims, case management, insurance, or government systems
 Experience with Azure DevOps and CI/CD for Power Platform solutions
 Benefits 
 Compensation: $75 to $85 per hour on a 1099 basis, depending on experience. W2 is also available.
 Contract length: approximately two years, with potential extension.
 Schedule: fully remote, U.S. based.
